citation.authors: Agarwal SK, Stokes M, Chen R, Lickert C

cited_by.title: Heavy periods by life stage and cause

record.population: 46,139 White and 17,297 Black women (commercial insurance) and 7,353 White and 16,776 Black women (Medicaid), US, with uterine fibroids and heavy menstrual bleeding
record.design: Retrospective cohort from insurance claims, 2010 to 2020
record.finding: Black women were diagnosed at a younger age; anaemia was more common (commercial 5.9% against 3.6%; Medicaid 7.0% against 4.5%). Hysterectomy was more common in White women (commercial 43.9% against 37.8%). About half stopped hormonal contraceptive treatment within about 5 months.
record.note: Claims data in insured people only; race as recorded in the database.
